info:
## Lesson 12 - the decoder, one instruction at a time

The slide switches select a real instruction, assembled by `tools/rvasm.py`, and the LEDs show eight of the control lines it produces. Nothing here is clocked: a decoder is a function of the instruction word and nothing else.

| sw3..sw0 | instruction | LEDs that light |
|---|---|---|
| 0000 | `addi x1, x0, 5` | we, imm |
| 0001 | `add x1, x2, x3` | we |
| 0010 | `sub x1, x2, x3` | we |
| 0011 | `lw x1, 0(x2)` | ld, we, imm |
| 0100 | `sw x1, 0(x2)` | sw, imm |
| 0101 | `beq x1, x2, -20` | branch |
| 0110 | `jal x1, -24` | jump, we, imm, pc |
| 0111 | `lui x1, 0x12345` | we, imm |
| 1xxx | `0xffffffff` | **illegal**, imm |

The LEDs, left to right, are `illegal`, `jump`, `branch`, `mem_write`, `mem_read`, `reg_we`, `alu_b_imm`, `alu_a_pc`.

### What to notice

`add` and `sub` light exactly the same lamps - verified in simulation, not by reading the source. The difference between them is not a control line at all - it is `inst[30]`, which rides into `alu_op` and changes what the ALU does, not what the datapath does. That is the decoder's whole design: say as little as possible, as early as possible.

Switch to any `1xxx` and `illegal` lights. Look at which lamps go out with it: `reg_we`, `mem_write`, `mem_read`, `branch` and `jump` - every line that **commits** something. An instruction the decoder does not recognise must not write a register, store a byte or move the PC, and that is exactly what you see.

`alu_b_imm` stays lit, which is worth understanding rather than worrying about: with nothing committing, whether operand B comes from the immediate or from rs2 changes no state at all. It is a don't-care, and the decoder spends no logic forcing don't-cares to zero.

### Why `inst` is not on pins

The decoder takes 32 bits in and produces 27 bits of control out. The board has 4 switches, 7 buttons and 8 LEDs, so the full interface is impossible by a factor of eight. The switches pick from a table instead, and the other 19 outputs are declared inside the block and left unconnected. This is the point at which schematic entry stops being the better view - which is why lessons 10 and up are editor-first, and why the lesson's own testbench drives all 32 bits: `cd 12-datapath && make sim`.
